source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.

1	# Architecture
2	
3	## Starting point
4	
5	Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:
6	
7	- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
8	  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
9	  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
10	  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
11	- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
12	  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
13	  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
14	- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
15	  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
16	  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
17	- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
18	  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
19	  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
20	  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
21	  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
22	  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
23	  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
24	- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
25	  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
26	  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
27	  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
28	  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
29	  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
30	  bodies to escaped rich text.
31	- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
32	  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
33	  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
34	  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
35	  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
36	  when only tags or highlight change.
37	- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
38	  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
39	  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
40	- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
41	  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
42	  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
43	  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
44	- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
45	  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
46	  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
47	  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
48	  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
49	  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
50	  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
51	  two imports.
52	- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
53	  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
54	  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
55	  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
56	  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
57	- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
58	  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
59	  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
60	  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
61	  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
62	  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
63	  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
64	  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
65	  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
66	  one from its note.
67	- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
68	  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
69	- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
70	  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
71	  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
72	  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
73	  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
74	  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
75	  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
76	  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
77	  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
78	- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
79	  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
80	  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
81	  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
82	  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
83	  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
84	  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
85	  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
86	  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
87	  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
88	  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
89	- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
90	  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
91	  credentials are configured.
92	- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
93	  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
94	  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
95	  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
96	  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
97	  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
98	- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
99	  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
100	  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
101	  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
102	  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
103	  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
104	  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
105	  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
106	- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
107	  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
108	  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
109	  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
110	- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
111	  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
112	  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
113	  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
114	  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
115	  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
116	  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
117	  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
118	  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
119	  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
120	- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
121	  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
122	  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
123	  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
124	- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
125	  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
126	  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
127	  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
128	  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
129	  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
130	  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
131	  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
132	  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
133	  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
134	- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
135	  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
136	  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
137	- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
138	  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
139	  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
140	  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
141	  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
142	  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
143	  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
144	  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
145	  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
146	- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
147	  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
148	  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
149	  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
150	  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not
151	  scheduled, scheduled, or sent. A job that fails after the email is written can
152	  send it again when Sidekiq retries it.
153	- Postponing moves the reminder 24 elapsed hours later. The note page previews
154	  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
155	  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,
156	  but at a different offset and wall-clock time from the postponed reminder.
157	- A reader requests a digest of their ready notes from the notes page
158	  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a
159	  Redis set for the request's UTC date
160	  (`digest_requests:YYYY-MM-DD`, kept for two days) and queues `DigestJob` with
161	  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
162	  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set
163	  is told the digest was already requested. If the job cannot be queued, the
164	  reservation is removed and the error raised, so the request fails and can be
165	  repeated. The reservation prevents repeated requests, not repeated emails:
166	  Sidekiq can run a job more than once. Each request logs redis-rb's deprecation
167	  warning for a single-member `sadd`, and Sidekiq warns that the job's arguments
168	  are not native JSON types, because of the `BigDecimal`.
169	- Sidekiq stores the job's arguments as JSON. Active Job 7.0 sends the request
170	  time with its UTC offset but deserializes it in the worker's zone, UTC, and the
171	  completion arrives as a decimal string such as `"0.6667"`. `DigestMailer` lists
172	  the reader's ready notes last updated during that UTC day, and dates the digest
173	  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.
174	  A digest is a snapshot when its job runs; notes updated afterward are not sent
175	  in a second digest for that UTC day.
176	- The mailers write plain-text email. Development writes each recipient's email
177	  to `tmp/mails` (Action Mailer's file delivery); tests use the `:test` delivery
178	  method. Production has no delivery method or link host configured.
179	- Active Storage serves blobs through signed URLs from its own controllers. Those
180	  URLs are not checked against the signed-in reader. The embedded blob redirect
181	  URLs do not expire, although the Disk-service URLs they redirect to do.
182	  The direct-upload controller checks CSRF, not sign-in; the public sign-in page
183	  supplies a CSRF token to anonymous clients. This sample has no private-file
184	  access policy or upload-abuse protection for a public deployment.
185	
186	These conventions guide further features without prescribing a schema in advance.
187	
188	The initial runtime is Ruby 3.3.6 and Rails 7.0.8.7 with Rails 7.0 defaults.
189	[Gemfile](Gemfile), [Gemfile.lock](Gemfile.lock), [.ruby-version](.ruby-version), and
190	[config/application.rb](config/application.rb) are the executable sources of truth.
191	
192	- PostgreSQL is the application database. Use Active Record and migrations for
193	  application-owned records, constraints, indexes, and transactions.
194	- ERB renders HTML. The generated app includes Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, and
195	  Stimulus. Jbuilder is available for requested JSON representations, but an HTML
196	  feature does not automatically need a JSON API.
197	- Rails includes the mailer, job, storage, and cable frameworks. Their presence
198	  does not mean broadcasts are implemented features. Email is sent only for
199	  reminders and digests, and is not delivered outside development's files. File
200	  uploads exist only as rich-text attachments.
201	- Active Job uses Sidekiq 6.5 as its adapter outside tests, so queued jobs are
202	  kept in Redis (`REDIS_URL`, by default `redis://localhost:6379`) and run in a
203	  separate `bundle exec sidekiq` process. Tests use Active Job's test adapter.
204	  `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job rather than an Active Job, so its job ID can
205	  be shown. Sidekiq stores its arguments as JSON, and it uses Sidekiq's default
206	  retries.
207	- Action Text 7.0.8.7 bundles Trix 1.3.4. That version cannot load saved HTML
208	  that has attributes, such as links or attachments, so the layout loads Trix
209	  1.3.5 from `vendor/javascript` as a classic script. Trix 1.x is not an ES
210	  module, so it is not in the import map. `@rails/actiontext` is.
211	  The vendored build comes from the [Trix 1.3.5 release](https://github.com/basecamp/trix/tree/1.3.5)
212	  and includes its [MIT license](vendor/javascript/trix-1.3.5.LICENSE).
213	- Orb setup starts PostgreSQL and Redis. Redis holds Sidekiq's queues and the
214	  digest reservations; it is not an application cache. The generated production
215	  cable configuration names Redis. That configuration is not a verified deployment.
216	
217	## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities
218	
219	Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:
220	
221	| Responsibility | Home |
222	| --- | --- |
223	| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
224	| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
225	| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
226	| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
227	| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
228	| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
229	| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
230	| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
231	| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
232	| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |
233	
234	A controller can call Active Record directly for a simple save. A multi-step
235	domain transition belongs behind a meaningful model method, not a sequence of
236	unrelated updates in the controller. Use a plain Ruby object or Active Model when
237	an operation needs its own object but no database table. Do not introduce a
238	mandatory service, repository, presenter, or command layer between every pair of
239	Rails objects.
240	
241	Fizzy models closing a card as a singular closure resource. Its controller calls
242	`Card#close`, and `Card::Closeable` owns the association, predicates, and transaction.
243	The [closure sources](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) illustrate a resource
244	boundary and a domain method, not a requirement to add cards to Margin Notes.
245	
246	## Model resources, not collections of verbs
247	
248	Use the conventional REST actions, including `new` and `edit` for HTML forms.
249	When a new operation does not fit an existing resource, look for the resource it
250	creates, updates, or removes before adding a custom action. Keep nesting shallow
251	enough that the parent conveys ownership rather than reproducing the whole schema.
252	
253	Use route helpers in views and responses. Controllers choose the representation.
254	Models do not construct controller responses or reach into request parameters.
255	
256	## Keep data ownership and effects explicit
257	
258	- PostgreSQL owns durable application facts. Derive a value from those facts
259	  unless storing it solves a demonstrated query, history, or concurrency need.
260	- Put invariants used outside HTTP in the domain model. Add database constraints
261	  when integrity must also hold across concurrent requests and non-model writes.
262	- Keep related database writes in one transaction. Do not assume it can undo a
263	  remote request, an email, or a job already sent to another system.
264	- Jobs should delegate to domain behavior and carry the identifiers or context
265	  they need. Decide retries, duplicate delivery, and transaction timing when a
266	  real background feature is introduced, rather than adding a queue preemptively.
267	- Keep network clients at visible boundaries. Preserve failure information and
268	  distinguish a legitimate empty response from a failed operation.
269	
270	Fizzy's [comment example](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) enforces comment
271	eligibility in both the model and the controller. Callers outside HTTP must obey
272	the same rule.
273	
274	## Authorization is not presentation
275	
276	Define ownership and the authorized lookup scope together. Resolve records
277	through the signed-in reader: `current_user.notebooks` and `current_user.notes`.
278	Direct lookups outside that scope raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is
279	a 404 in production. A submitted `notebook_id` is resolved through
280	`current_user.notebooks.find_by`, never assigned directly. A missing or foreign
281	notebook fails validation and renders the form with 422, without saving the note.
282	Resolve nested records through their authorized parent. Neither an unguessable ID
283	nor a hidden or disabled button grants or checks permission.
284	
285	Keep actor-dependent decisions explicit in domain APIs and reusable rendering.
286	If request-local state is introduced, set and reset it at the request boundary.
287	Jobs, mailers, and tests must not rely on a previous request having populated it.
288	Do not adopt a tenancy or identity scheme solely because a reference application
289	uses one.
290	
291	## Render on the server, enhance in the browser
292	
293	Use HTML forms and links for their native semantics. Turbo handles navigation,
294	frames, and targeted replacements. Stimulus supplies local interaction that HTML
295	does not provide. Keep persistence and authorization on the server, not in a
296	second client-side model of the domain.
297	
298	Partials take the resources and presentation inputs they need. A template may
299	compose several resources. A reusable partial should not depend on a particular
300	controller's incidental instance variables or on undeclared request context.
301	See the [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) for HTML, accessibility, Turbo, and JSON.
302	
303	## Optimize the actual representation
304	
305	Start with correct queries and clear response contracts. Filter and order before
306	pagination. Use a stable tie-breaker where page membership must be deterministic.
307	Load the associations that the rendered representation uses rather than adding
308	a universal preload list to every request.
309	
310	Define cache keys and invalidation rules before introducing caching. Include
311	permissions, locale, and related-record changes when they affect the output, or
312	keep those parts outside the shared fragment. The
313	[board example](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) illustrates why a
314	warm cache must be tested with another viewer, not just the same request twice.
315	
316	## Scope and reference boundaries
317	
318	The [public examples](docs/references/fizzy.md) are evidence for design ideas, not
319	a compatible application template. Their Ruby, Rails, database adapters, asset
320	pipeline, editors, and helper libraries differ from this repository. Use the
321	locked local APIs, and introduce new infrastructure only for a requested feature.
322	
323	As features land, document their ownership and invariants here. Keep detailed
324	layer practices in the [model](docs/guides/models.md),
325	[controller](docs/guides/controllers.md), and [view](docs/guides/views.md) guides,
326	and verification rules in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

382	
383	Read the relevant [task skill](CLAUDE.md#task-skills) and its guide. Start with the
384	existing route, model, representation, and test closest to the requested change.
385	For a new feature, build a small working path through these layers before adding
386	abstractions for hypothetical variants.

389	case. For a bug, reproduce the wrong result before changing its implementation
390	when practical. Keep refactoring separate from a deliberate contract change.
391	
392	Run focused tests while working, then the broader commands in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

398	
399	- Inspect the complete diff, including generated files and dependency changes.

401	  make a check pass without understanding what it contains.
402	- Keep commits coherent. Explain behavior and non-obvious choices rather than

408	# Testing
409	
410	## Test the contract at its boundary
411	
412	Use Rails' Minitest integration with real application objects and the test
413	PostgreSQL database. Exercise the route, controller, model, and rendering stack
414	for HTTP behavior. When needed, substitute a controlled response at an external
415	boundary. Do not stub the domain behavior under test.
416	
417	Choose the smallest boundary that can catch the likely mistake:
418	
419	| Contract | Test |
420	| --- | --- |
421	| A domain decision, transition, or query | `ActiveSupport::TestCase` in `test/models/` |
422	| Routing, permissions, persistence, HTML, Turbo, or JSON | `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` in `test/controllers/` |
423	| A workflow across endpoints | An integration test in `test/integration/` |
424	| Browser execution, focus, navigation, or JavaScript interaction | `ApplicationSystemTestCase` in `test/system/` |
425	| Scheduling, delivery, and job-specific failure behavior | Rails job and mailer test helpers, usually in the request test that queues the job |
426	
427	Do not add a separate test for every method. Prefer assertions that would survive
428	an internal refactor. A useful regression test fails for a plausible wrong
429	implementation, not just a syntax error.
430	
431	## Commands and current configuration
432	
433	Use only a disposable test database. Rails may create, reload, or replace its
434	data. Never point test configuration at development data you need to keep, a
435	shared environment, or production.
436	
437	Run commands from the repository root with the pinned Ruby active:
438	
439	```sh
440	bundle check
441	bin/rails zeitwerk:check
442	bin/rails test
443	bin/rails test:system
444	```
445	
446	`bin/rails test` does not include system tests. The generated
447	[system test base](test/application_system_test_case.rb) uses Selenium with Chrome,
448	not headless Chrome. Until that configuration changes, system tests require a
449	display and a suitable browser and driver.
450	
451	For focused feedback, run a test directory:
452	
453	```sh
454	bin/rails test test/controllers
455	bin/rails test test/models
456	```
457	
458	To run one file, pass its path to `bin/rails test`. Append `:LINE` to that path to
459	select a test.
460	
461	The Gemfile keeps Minitest on 5.x because Rails 7.0's test runner fails under
462	Minitest 6. No RuboCop, security-audit command, or `bin/ci` is configured.
463	
464	[test/test_helper.rb](test/test_helper.rb) loads all fixtures and configures
465	processor-count parallel workers.
466	
467	The [test environment](config/environments/test.rb) disables caching and raises
468	application exceptions. For error-response or cache tests, set the required mode
469	explicitly and restore it afterward. Do not assume production behavior. The mail
470	delivery method is `:test`.
471	
472	## Make scenarios distinguish the right behavior
473	
474	- Name the domain fact or user outcome: a rejected edit leaves the body unchanged,
475	  not merely that an update action runs.
476	- Keep arrangement, action, and assertions recognizable. Share setup only for
477	  facts every test in that group needs. Do not hide the decisive input in a helper.
478	- Establish meaningful preconditions when the operation could otherwise be a
479	  no-op. Reload records when checking what was persisted.
480	- Use asymmetric values and contrasting records. A permission test needs another
481	  user's record. A filter needs both an included and an excluded candidate.
482	- Derive expected results independently. Do not call the production scope or
483	  serializer to compute the value the same scope or serializer should return.
484	- Assert order only where ordering is promised. For membership, include/exclude
485	  assertions can express the rule better than an exact count of unrelated fixtures.
486	  Assert total counts when pagination, duplicates, or filtering totals are contractual.
487	- Test both a successful result and the relevant failure or boundary. A denial
488	  should check that no unauthorized write or side effect occurred.
489	
490	Fizzy's [closure tests](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) combine an initially
491	open card, a state change, and recorded actor/event information. Its
492	[comment request tests](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) check that someone
493	cannot edit another person's comment and that the stored body remains unchanged.
494	Those are behavioral contracts, not expectations about private method calls.
495	
496	## Fixtures and time
497	
498	Use named, coherent fixtures for shared test data. Change or build a record inside
499	a test when the variation belongs to that scenario alone. See the
500	[fixture guide](docs/guides/fixtures.md) before adding shared data.
501	
502	For time-sensitive behavior, freeze or travel to an explicit instant using Rails'
503	test helpers and exercise the boundary from both sides. Do not make a test depend
504	on the current wall clock, execution order, or an arbitrary first fixture.
505	
506	Keep expected text, dates, IDs, and permission outcomes visible where they explain
507	the test. Helpers should remove setup mechanics, not choose expected results.
508	
509	## Requests and representations
510	
511	Use real verbs, route helpers, and request formats. Check status and the important
512	response contract as well as persistence: redirect destination, `Location`, field
513	values, absent versus null fields, or the relevant rendered controls.
514	
515	For HTML, use `assert_select` for semantic elements, labels, error messages, and
516	form targets. For JSON, assert the intended public representation rather than the
517	whole Active Record attribute hash. For Turbo streams, check the action, target,
518	and meaningful content. A stream response does not prove the browser applied it.
519	
520	For a browser interaction, drive the visible UI and wait on an observable result
521	instead of sleeping. Include the failure or non-default state the change affects.
522	Inspect the rendered result at representative widths when appearance changes.
523	
524	The [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) distinguishes ordinary forms, enhanced
525	submissions, and interactions that genuinely require browser coverage.
526	
527	## Queries and caches
528	
529	An N+1 regression needs several parent records with different associated records.
530	Measure the query work inside the request or operation, not fixture loading.
531	Use the database and supported instrumentation; do not assert private ORM calls
532	or assume helpers from another repository exist here.
533	
534	For cache tests, enable caching and use a test-local store. Restore the store and
535	settings in `ensure` or teardown. Exercise a miss, a hit, a relevant data change,
536	and a contrasting viewer when output varies by permission. A repeat request with
537	caching disabled proves nothing about a cache.
538	
539	Fizzy's [board tests](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) request the same
540	settings as privileged and unprivileged users with partial caching enabled. The
541	assertion concerns the disabled control, not merely the number of cache calls.
542	Fizzy's helper uses renderer internals and is not a drop-in helper for this Rails
543	version.
544	
545	## External effects and asynchronous work
546	
547	Use Rails' job and mailer test helpers for enqueuing/delivery contracts. A test of
548	enqueueing does not establish successful job execution. Exercise domain behavior
549	separately, and execute the job when its context, serialization, or retries matter.
550	
551	Native Sidekiq jobs such as `ExportJob` do not use the Active Job adapter.
552	[test/test_helper.rb](test/test_helper.rb) loads Sidekiq's fake testing mode, which
553	keeps each pushed job in memory after a JSON round trip, as Redis would. Assert
554	`ExportJob.jobs` for the enqueued arguments, call `ExportJob.drain` to run them,
555	and clear them in setup.
556	
557	The Active Job test adapter serializes arguments, but does not round-trip them
558	through JSON as Sidekiq does: a `BigDecimal` argument stays a `BigDecimal` in
559	tests and arrives as a string in a worker. A time with zone is deserialized in
560	UTC in both.
561	
562	Digest requests reserve the reader in a real Redis set, so those tests need Redis
563	(`REDIS_URL`, by default `redis://localhost:6379`). Set `REDIS_URL` to a disposable
564	Redis database separate from development, for example
565	`REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/1 bin/rails test`. Reservations are outside the
566	database transaction, so each test releases the readers and dates it uses before
567	starting, and uses dates no other test uses. A refused enqueue is substituted at
568	the queue boundary with Minitest's `stub`.
569	
570	Keep remote services out of ordinary tests. The citation enrichment tests serve
571	scripted responses from a loopback HTTP server in the test process, so Faraday's
572	retry and authentication run for real without an external service. One test boots
573	a fresh Rails process to verify environment credentials before configuration is
574	cached. Use a local fake or an already available substitution facility at the
575	client boundary. Do not introduce a mocking library just to avoid constructing a
576	model, and do not record real tokens or personal data in fixtures or HTTP recordings.
577	
578	## Report evidence accurately
579	
580	Report the command, result, and scope. Separate tests that passed from tests not
581	run, environment failures, skipped cases, and manual browser checks. A source
582	example or an inspected test is not a test result for Margin Notes.
583	# Margin Notes
584	
585	A full-stack Rails reading-notebook application. Readers sign in, keep private
586	notebooks, and write rich-text notes with small attachments, tags, a highlight
587	color, and a draft/ready status. The note list at `/notes` (also bookmarked as
588	`/journal`) supports title search and notebook and status filters. Each notebook
589	has settings for its name and export heading, and a slug fixed at creation. The app uses Ruby 3.3.6, Rails 7.0.8.7, PostgreSQL, and Rails'
590	generated importmap/Turbo/Stimulus frontend.
591	
592	A reader can import notes into a notebook from a UTF-8 CSV file of up to 100
593	notes and 100 KB, with this header row:
594	
595	```csv
596	title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch
597	```
598	
599	Only `title` is required. `body_html` becomes the rich-text body. A `doi` looks
600	like `10.1234/example`. `annotation` is the reader's plain-text comment on the
601	citation, and `reminder_epoch` is a time in seconds since 1970 (UTC). An imported
602	reminder is scheduled from its note. The import shows a preview with each row's
603	source line and errors before anything is saved, then imports all rows or none.
604	
605	A DOI can also be entered on the note form. From a note's page, a reader can fetch
606	the cited work's title and source URL from a citation metadata provider. The page
607	shows whether that request is pending, completed, or failed. Citations, and so
608	their metadata, are shared by every reader who cites the same DOI. Requests run in
609	a Sidekiq worker; development uses a local stand-in provider (see
610	[Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#prepare-the-environment)).
611	
612	A reader can export a notebook as a Markdown file. The export runs in the
613	Sidekiq worker; its page shows whether it is queued, working, complete, or
614	cancelled, how many notes it has processed, and its job ID. A queued or working
615	export can be cancelled. A completed file can be downloaded for 24 hours.
616	
617	Each notebook has an activity page listing how many of its notes were created on
618	each UTC date, newest first, skipping dates without notes. It counts the notes the
619	notebook has now, so it is not a permanent history: a deleted note is no longer
620	counted.
621	
622	A reader can schedule an email reminder for a note at a date and time in their
623	time zone, chosen on the account settings page, and postpone it by a day. From
624	the notes page, a reader can request an email digest of the ready notes updated
625	that day, once per UTC day. The digest's day and the request limit both use the
626	UTC date of the request, which can differ from the reader's date near midnight.
627	Email is written to files in
628	development rather than sent (see [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#prepare-the-environment)).
629	
630	`bin/rails db:seed` creates two development readers, `reader@example.com` and
631	`other@example.com`, each with the password `password`. There is no registration
632	or password recovery.

730	#!/usr/bin/env ruby
731	# A deterministic local stand-in for the citation metadata provider, for
732	# development and demonstrations. It never contacts a real service.
733	#
734	#   GET /works?doi=10.1234/example with basic authentication answers
735	#   {"title": "Sample record for 10.1234/example", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1234/example"}
736	#
737	# Wrong or missing credentials get 401. These DOI endings simulate failures:
738	#
739	#   /not-found          404
740	#   /unavailable        503 on every request
741	#   /unavailable-once   503 on the first request since this server started, then 200
742	#
743	# Settings: CITATION_PROVIDER_PORT (default 9393), CITATION_PROVIDER_USER and
744	# CITATION_PROVIDER_PASSWORD (defaults match config/secrets.yml for development).
745	require "bundler/setup"
746	require "erb"
747	require "json"
748	require "set"
749	require "rack"
750	require "rack/handler/puma"
751	
752	port = Integer(ENV.fetch("CITATION_PROVIDER_PORT", "9393"))
753	credentials = [ENV.fetch("CITATION_PROVIDER_USER", "margin-notes"), ENV.fetch("CITATION_PROVIDER_PASSWORD", "local-only")]
754	failed_once = Set.new
755	lock = Mutex.new
756	
757	app = lambda do |env|
758	  request = Rack::Request.new(env)
759	  auth = Rack::Auth::Basic::Request.new(env)
760	  doi = request.params["doi"].to_s
761	
762	  status =
763	    if !(auth.provided? && auth.basic? && auth.credentials == credentials) then 401
764	    elsif !request.get? || request.path != "/works" || doi.empty? || doi.end_with?("/not-found") then 404
765	    elsif doi.end_with?("/unavailable") then 503
766	    elsif doi.end_with?("/unavailable-once") && lock.synchronize { failed_once.add?(doi) } then 503
767	    else 200
768	    end
769	
770	  body =
771	    if status == 200
772	      { title: "Sample record for #{doi}", url: "https://doi.org/#{doi.split("/").map { |part| ERB::Util.url_encode(part) }.join("/")}" }
773	    else
774	      { error: Rack::Utils::HTTP_STATUS_CODES[status] }
775	    end
776	
777	  $stdout.puts "#{Time.now.utc.iso8601(3)} #{request.request_method} #{request.fullpath} -> #{status}"
778	  $stdout.flush
779	  [status, { "Content-Type" => "application/json" }, [body.to_json]]
780	end
781	
782	# "-" keeps Puma from loading the application server's config/puma.rb.
783	Rack::Handler::Puma.run(app, Host: "127.0.0.1", Port: port, Threads: "0:4", config_files: ["-"])

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end
        end
        enqueued_count
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # == Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter
      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        # Sidekiq::Client does not support symbols as keys
        job.provider_job_id = Sidekiq::Client.push \
          "class"   => JobWrapper,
          "wrapped" => job.class,
          "queue"   => job.queue_name,
          "args"    => [ job.serialize ]
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = Sidekiq::Client.push \
          "class"   => JobWrapper,
          "wrapped" => job.class,
          "queue"   => job.queue_name,
          "args"    => [ job.serialize ],
          "at"      => timestamp
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Active Job Abstract Adapter
    #
    # Active Job supports multiple job queue systems. ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::AbstractAdapter
    # forms the abstraction layer which makes this possible.
    class AbstractAdapter
      attr_accessor :stopping

      def enqueue(job)
        raise NotImplementedError

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp)
        raise NotImplementedError
      end

      def stopping?
        !!@stopping
      end
    end
  end

        end

# Loads default configuration values for a target version. This includes
      # defaults for versions prior to the target version. See the
      # {configuration guide}[https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#versioned-default-values]
      # for the default values associated with a particular version.
      def load_defaults(target_version)
        # To introduce a change in behavior, follow these steps:
        # 1. Add an accessor on the target object (e.g. the ActiveJob class for
        #    global Active Job config).
        # 2. Set a default value there preserving existing behavior for existing
        #    applications.
        # 3. Implement the behavior change based on the config value.
        # 4. In the section below corresponding to the next release of Rails,
        #    configure the default value.
        # 5. Add a commented out section in the `new_framework_defaults` to
        #    configure the default value again.
        # 6. Update the guide in `configuring.md`.

        # To remove configurable deprecated behavior, follow these steps:
        # 1. Update or remove the entry in the guides.
        # 2. Remove the references below.
        # 3. Remove the legacy code paths and config check.
        # 4. Remove the config accessor.

        case target_version.to_s
        when "5.0"
          if respond_to?(:action_controller)
            action_controller.per_form_csrf_tokens = true
            action_controller.forgery_protection_origin_check = true
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_record)
            action_mailer.deliver_later_queue_name = nil
          end

          ActiveSupport.utc_to_local_returns_utc_offset_times = true
        when "7.0"
          load_defaults "6.1"

          if respond_to?(:action_dispatch)
            action_dispatch.default_headers = {
              "X-Frame-Options" => "SAMEORIGIN",
              "X-XSS-Protection" => "0",
              "X-Content-Type-Options" => "nosniff",
              "X-Download-Options" => "noopen",
              "X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies" => "none",
              "Referrer-Policy" => "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
            }
            action_dispatch.cookies_serializer = :json
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_view)
            action_view.button_to_generates_button_tag = true
            action_view.apply_stylesheet_media_default = false
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_support)
            active_support.hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256
            active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256
            active_support.cache_format_version = 7.0
            active_support.executor_around_test_case = true
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_mailer)
            action_mailer.smtp_timeout = 5
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_storage)
            active_storage.video_preview_arguments =
              "-vf 'select=eq(n\\,0)+eq(key\\,1)+gt(scene\\,0.015),loop=loop=-1:size=2,trim=start_frame=1'" \
              " -frames:v 1 -f image2"

            active_storage.variant_processor = :vips
            active_storage.multiple_file_field_include_hidden = true
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_record)
            active_record.verify_foreign_keys_for_fixtures = true
            active_record.partial_inserts = false
            active_record.automatic_scope_inversing = true
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_controller)
            action_controller.action_on_open_redirect = :raise
            action_controller.wrap_parameters_by_default = true
          end
        when "7.1"
          load_defaults "7.0"

          self.add_autoload_paths_to_load_path = false
          self.precompile_filter_parameters = true
          self.dom_testing_default_html_version = defined?(Nokogiri::HTML5) ? :html5 : :html4

          if Rails.env.local?
            self.log_file_size = 100 * 1024 * 1024
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_record)
            active_record.run_commit_callbacks_on_first_saved_instances_in_transaction = false
            active_record.sqlite3_adapter_strict_strings_by_default = true
            active_record.query_log_tags_format = :sqlcommenter
            active_record.raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly = true
            active_record.belongs_to_required_validates_foreign_key = false
            active_record.before_committed_on_all_records = true
            active_record.default_column_serializer = nil
            active_record.encryption.hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256
            active_record.encryption.support_sha1_for_non_deterministic_encryption = false
            active_record.marshalling_format_version = 7.1
            active_record.run_after_transaction_callbacks_in_order_defined = true
            active_record.generate_secure_token_on = :initialize
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_dispatch)
            action_dispatch.default_headers = {
              "X-Frame-Options" => "SAMEORIGIN",
              "X-XSS-Protection" => "0",
              "X-Content-Type-Options" => "nosniff",
              "X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies" => "none",

            action_dispatch.debug_exception_log_level = :error

          if respond_to?(:active_support)

            active_support.message_serializer = :json_allow_marshal

          end

        when "8.1"

          # redefine methods (e.g. mocking), hence YJIT isn't generally
          # faster in these environments.
          self.yjit = !Rails.env.local?

            action_controller.escape_json_responses = false
            action_controller.action_on_path_relative_redirect = :raise
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_record)
            active_record.raise_on_missing_required_finder_order_columns = true
          end

          if respond_to?(:active_support)
            active_support.escape_js_separators_in_json = false
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_view)
            action_view.render_tracker = :ruby
          end

          if respond_to?(:action_view)
            action_view.remove_hidden_field_autocomplete = true
          end
        else
          raise "Unknown version #{target_version.to_s.inspect}"
        end

        @loaded_config_version = target_version
      end

      def reloading_enabled?
        enable_reloading
      end

      def enable_reloading
        !cache_classes
      end

      def enable_reloading=(value)
        self.cache_classes = !value
      end

      def encoding=(value)
        @encoding = value

def fetch_value(name, &block)
      if attr = @attributes[name]
        return attr.value(&block)
      end

      @casted_values.fetch(name) do
        value_present = true
        value = values.fetch(name) { value_present = false }

        if value_present
          type = additional_types.fetch(name, types[name])
          @casted_values[name] = type.deserialize(value)
        else
          attr = default_attribute(name, value_present, value)
          attr.value(&block)
        end
      end
    end

    protected
      def attributes
        unless @materialized
          values.each_key { |key| self[key] }
          types.each_key { |key| self[key] }
          @materialized = true
        end
        @attributes
      end

    private
      attr_reader :values, :types, :additional_types, :default_attributes

      def default_attribute(
        name,
        value_present = true,
        copy.instance_variable_set(:@delegate_hash, delegate_hash.transform_values(&:dup))
      end
    end

    def initialize_dup(_)
      @delegate_hash = Hash[delegate_hash]
      super
    end

    def each_key(&block)
      keys = types.keys | values.keys | delegate_hash.keys
      keys.each(&block)
    end

    def ==(other)
      if other.is_a?(LazyAttributeHash)
        materialize == other.materialize
      else
        materialize == other
      end
    end

    def sanitizer_allowed_attributes
      allowed_attributes || (sanitizer.class.allowed_attributes + ActionText::Attachment::ATTRIBUTES)
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    private
      def raw_enqueue
        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit
          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self
        else
          super
        end
      end
  end
end
  module Enqueuing
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      ##
      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.
      #
      # Returns an instance of the job class queued with arguments available in
      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #
      # If Active Job is used conjointly with Active Record, and #perform_later is called
      # inside an Active Record transaction, then the enqueue is implicitly deferred to after
      # the transaction is committed, or dropped if it's rolled back. In such case #perform_later
      # will return the job instance like if it was successfully enqueued, but will still return
      # +false+ if a callback prevented the job from being enqueued.
      #
      # This behavior can be changed on a per job basis:
      #
      #  class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      #    self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false
      #  end
      def perform_later(...)
        job = job_or_instantiate(...)
        enqueue_result = job.enqueue

        yield job if block_given?

        enqueue_result
      end

      private
      else
        false
      end
    end

    private
      def raw_enqueue
        run_callbacks :enqueue do
          _raw_enqueue
        end
      end

      def _raw_enqueue
        if scheduled_at
          queue_adapter.enqueue_at self, scheduled_at.to_f
        else
          queue_adapter.enqueue self
        end

        self.successfully_enqueued = true
      rescue EnqueueError => e
        self.enqueue_error = e
      end
  end
end

*   Bring back the historical behavior of committing transaction on non-local return.

    ```ruby
    Model.transaction do
      model.save
      return
      other_model.save # not executed
    end
    ```

    Historically only raised errors would trigger a rollback, but in Ruby `2.3`, the `timeout` library
    started using `throw` to interrupt execution which had the adverse effect of committing open transactions.

    To solve this, in Active Record 6.1 the behavior was changed to instead rollback the transaction as it was safer
    than to potentially commit an incomplete transaction.

    Using `return`, `break` or `throw` inside a `transaction` block was essentially deprecated from Rails 6.1 onwards.

content.content:
*   Serialized attributes can now be marked as comparable.

    A not rare issue when working with serialized attributes is that the serialized representation of an object
    can change over time. Either because you are migrating from one serializer to the other (e.g. YAML to JSON or to msgpack),
    or because the serializer used subtly changed its output.

    One example is libyaml that used to have some extra trailing whitespaces, and recently fixed that.
    When this sorts of thing happen, you end up with lots of records that report being changed even though
    they aren't, which in the best case leads to a lot more writes to the database and in the worst case lead to nasty bugs.

    The solution is to instead compare the deserialized representation of the object, however Active Record
    can't assume the deserialized object has a working `==` method. Hence why this new functionality is opt-in.

    ```ruby
    serialize :config, type: Hash, coder: JSON, comparable: true
    ```

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Fix MySQL default functions getting dropped when changing a column's nullability.
*   The table columns inside `schema.rb` are now sorted alphabetically.

    Previously they'd be sorted by creation order, which can cause merge conflicts when two
    branches modify the same table concurrently.

    *John Duff*

*   Introduce versions formatter for the schema dumper.
*   Use `_N` as a parallel tests databases suffixes

    Peviously, `-N` was used as a suffix. This can cause problems for RDBMSes
    which do not support dashes in database names.

    *fatkodima*

    is helpful if a bug is fixed in an analyzer or a new analyzer is added.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
